ICFI should be tracked as a small-cap federal cyber/compliance automation candidate; key survival test is evidence of defense-prime or DoD supplier-risk/compliance workflows rather than generic consulting exposure.

Most pure-play defense supply-chain illumination vendors appear private, including many supplier-mapping, sanctions, OSINT, and third-party-risk platforms; public-market mapping may require proxies in federal services, data analytics, cyber compliance, and procurement workflow software.

Dun & Bradstreet remains a strong private-company reference for the node because D&B Protect explicitly addresses public-sector subtier supplier visibility, but it should not be included in current US-listed candidate universes after the August 26, 2025 take-private transaction.

node: Defense subtier supply-chain visibility, mapping, compliance, and vendor-risk systems
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the defense subtier supply-chain illumination node found a narrow public-market universe. The strongest underfollowed mappings are not weapons primes but federal technology, compliance, cyber-risk, and supplier-risk data vendors. Parsons and ICF fit the preferred small/mid-cap lane through defense/federal cyber, acquisition, risk-management, and compliance workflows. FiscalNote is a speculative micro-cap exception because it explicitly markets AI-enabled mapping of suppliers and wider stakeholder risk, including military/government supply-chain use cases, but public-market viability and defense revenue concentration require verification. S&P Global is included only as a large reference benchmark for supplier-risk data products, not as the main alpha lane. Dun & Bradstreet appears highly relevant at the product level but was excluded from candidates because it was taken private in August 2025.
